topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causation.

topics.label: Origins of cancer: endogenous factors, genetic predisposition, and environmental epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multi-factorial origins of cancer, examining the relative contributions of endogenous biological processes, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures evidenced by population epidemiology.

topics.label: Infectious agents and the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how oncogenic pathogens contribute to cancer development, illustrated through the discovery and mechanism of Epstein-Barr virus and malaria in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical, dietary, and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biochemical pathways through which physical agents, dietary toxins, and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation and induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and host tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain non-mutagenic mechanisms in carcinogenesis, focusing on the roles of tumor promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental timing in malignant transformation.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and mutational signatures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogen exposure and evaluate carcinogenic potential.

topics.label: Lecture summary and risk-benefit analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a synthesis of environmental carcinogenesis concepts and final thoughts on personal risk-benefit decisions.
